claim:
For the success probability in Eq. (18) of El Allati--Hassouni--Metwally's entangled coherent quantum network, let \(m\ge2\), \(x=|\alpha|^2\ge0\), and \(a=2^{m-1}\). With the continuous value \(P_m(0)=1/2\), the formula simplifies exactly to
\[
P_m(x)=\frac12\frac{1+e^{-2(2a-1)x}}{1+e^{-2ax}}.
\]
It has a unique global minimum. Writing \(q_m=e^{-2x_m}\), the minimizer is characterized by the unique root \(q_m\in(0,1)\) of
\[
(2a-1)q_m^{a-1}+(a-1)q_m^{2a-1}=a.
\]
As \(m\to\infty\), the minimum forms a dyadic low-intensity boundary layer:
\[
2^m x_m\to\log(1+\sqrt2),\qquad \min_{x\ge0}P_m(x)\to\sqrt2-1.
\]
More generally, for every fixed \(t\ge0\),
\[
P_m(t/2^m)\to \frac12\frac{1+e^{-2t}}{1+e^{-t}}.
\]
Consequently \(P_m(x)\to1/2\) for every fixed \(x\ge0\), but the convergence is not uniform on \([0,\infty)\):
\[
\sup_{x\ge0}|P_m(x)-1/2|\to \frac32-\sqrt2.
\]
Thus the large-network field-intensity independence stated qualitatively in the source is pointwise: a shrinking window of width \(\Theta(2^{-m})\) retains a nonvanishing worst-case deficit.
integrity: The analytic proof establishes uniqueness and all asymptotic limits. The included finite computation is supplementary and is not used as an exhaustive or infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem analyzes the published success-probability formula in Eq. (18); it does not independently certify the complete optical derivation or experimental implementation, and it makes no claim about other teleportation architectures.
title: A dyadic boundary layer in coherent-network teleportation success probability
